data.name: Eiham
data.gender_notes: Eiham is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: This name means 'life' in Arabic. It is derived from the root word 'hayah' which means 'to live'. This name is a reminder of the preciousness of life and the importance of cherishing each moment. The name Eiham carries the meaning “Life” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Eiham usually hope their child will grow to embody life and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Eiham is a spiritual name that represents the essence of life. It is a reminder of the transient nature of existence and the importance of living in the present moment. It is a name that inspires a deep appreciation for the beauty and complexity of life and the universe.
data.etymology: Eiham belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Life.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Eiham total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_hindi.name: एहाम
in_hindi.meaning: एहाम का अर्थ है संकेत या चिह्न
in_hindi.long_meaning: एहाम नाम अरबी मूल 'هم' से निकला है जिसका अर्थ है संकेत या चिह्न। यह नाम भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में उस व्यक्ति के लिए प्रयोग किया जाता है जो गहरी अर्थों की ओर संकेत करता है। इस्लामी परंपरा में इसका उपयोग आध्यात्मिक संकेतों या प्रतीकों के संदर्भ में किया जाता है।

in_english.name: Eiham
in_english.meaning: Eiham means indication or hinting at something
in_english.long_meaning: The name Eiham is derived from the Arabic root 'هم' (ham) which means to indicate or hint at something. In Islamic culture, Eiham is used for a person who suggests or alludes to deep meanings. The Quran references signs or verses that hint at monotheism or the afterlife, reflecting the name's spiritual significance. Historically, the name has been used across various Muslim cultures to signify a person of profound insight or spiritual indication.
